chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from the Truthful (Al-Sadiq) Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Blessed is the one who abandons a present lust for a promised reward he has not yet seen."
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to abandon present lust for a promised reward in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual discipline of *zuhd* (asceticism) by prioritizing the unseen promise over visible gratification. It reflects the Shia emphasis on aligning human nature with divine will through conscious restraint, a virtue deeply rooted in the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt. This concept serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate patience and focus on eternal success amidst worldly trials.
